proposals.evidence: LSI niŋga pōnira “You went” contains a separate pronoun and inflected verb. DEDR 3688 records Kodagu niŋga “you” plural. DEDR 4572 quotes Kodagu po·- (po·p-, po·c-; also po·k-, po·y-) “go”; the source’s present pōp- and past pōc- are family members. Ordered links preserve the source word boundary and do not treat the sentence as a single inherited stem. LSI pōn- past differs from the Kodagu po·c- past quoted in DEDR 4572; the go-root identification is stronger than the tense-stem match.
